newsitem.title: USA: US House Banking's Leach sees Fed structure review.
newsitem.headline: US House Banking's Leach sees Fed structure review.

text.p: U.S. House Banking Committee Chairman James Leach said Wednesday he expects the panel will hear testimony this summer on making the Federal Reserve more open to the public.
The Iowa Republican also told reporters he was not surprised that Fed policymakers held interest rates steady at their Tuesday meeting, calling that decision "prudential."

"Their first move (a March 25 rate hike) had a more significant effect than they might have expected, and a second move at this time might have been counterproductive. I thought the Fed (Open Market Committee) was very prudential in not moving to increase rates at this time."
Leach, after a briefing by Chicago Fed President Michael Moskow, said he favors continuing movement toward more timely disclosure of monetary policy discussions.
"I believe in very steady movements toward greater democratization of Fed processes," Leach said, adding that he expected that "during the next year and a half we will see developments in this area."
Asked if he favored accelerated release of FOMC meeting minutes, which are currently disseminated after the ensuing meeting, Leach responded, "Oh yes, absolutely."

Leach noted that he continues to support an independent central bank free of day-to-day political concerns and reiterated his desire to shift the selection of regional Fed bank presidents to the Fed board in Washington from the regional banks.
"I believe the Federal Reserve district (presidents) ... ought to be appointed by the central Fed instead of elected by boards of directors at the local level," Leach said.
The Chicago Fed's Moskow, when asked about Leach's views on the selection of regional presidents, respectfully disagreed.
"I have a very high regard for Chairman Leach," Moskow said. But he added, "you have to be very careful when you make any changes in (Fed) structure," which can have "unforeseen circumstances."
